questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Ride more slowly than usual.
Start slowing down earlier than usual.
Increase your distance from the vehicle ahead.
Avoid talking to your passenger while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid talking to your passenger while riding.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle, which makes it respond more slowly. You should ride slower, start slowing sooner, and leave more distance from other vehicles. Always warn your passenger about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: Curved mirrors on most motorcycles:

options.text: Are easy to use right away.
Make cars look closer than they are.
Show only a narrow view of the road.
Make cars look farther away than they are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make cars look farther away than they are.
questions.explanation: Curved mirrors give you a wider view than flat mirrors. However, they make objects appear farther away than they really are. Practice judging distances if you are not used to curved mirrors.

questions.question: A rectangular sign can be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs with white background and black letters show road rules, such as speed limits. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: What helps you ride safely on slippery surfaces?

options.text: Using only the front brake.
Using both brakes.
Riding in the center of the lane.
Keeping or speeding up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using both brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down, use both brakes, and avoid sudden movements. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars, not in the center of the lane. Watch for oil spots and loose gravel.

questions.question: When turning, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through the turn.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: Riding clothes should protect you from all of the following, except:

options.text: Sunburn.
Windburn.
Chapped lips.
Dehydration.

questions.correctAnswerText: Chapped lips.
questions.explanation: Riding clothes should protect you from sunburn, windburn, rain, dehydration, cold, and the motorcycle. Good clothing also protects you if you crash.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks during braking on dry pavement, you should:

options.text: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake, then apply it again quickly.
Release the rear brake and downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If the rear brake locks on dry pavement, keep it locked until you stop. Your motorcycle will stay under control if it is upright and moving straight.

questions.question: Riding on the far side of a lane while following another vehicle:

options.text: Is recommended because drivers will see you easily.
Is not recommended because drivers rarely check their side mirrors.
Is recommended because a passenger might tell the driver you are there.
Is illegal because you must ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because drivers rarely check their side mirrors.
questions.explanation: Drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. Ride in the center of the lane to be visible in the driver's rearview mirror.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Ride a little more slowly than usual.
Start slowing down earlier than usual when stopping.
Wait for larger gaps in traffic before merging.
Speed up faster than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up faster than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight and changes how your motorcycle handles. It will accelerate slower, turn slower, and need more space to stop.

questions.question: The best protection for a motorcycle rider is:

options.text: Keeping distance between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
Wearing a good leather jacket.
Wearing sturdy boots.
Understanding motorcycle laws.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeping distance between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid crashes is to stay far away from other vehicles. This gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. Wearing proper safety gear is also important.

questions.question: When you must both brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Do both actions at the same time with extra braking pressure.
Do both actions at the same time, but focus mainly on swerving.
Do neither action.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: You need good traction to swerve safely. Do not brake and swerve at the same time. Instead, do one action first, then the other.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power comes from the front brake?

options.text: About 25 percent
About 50 percent
About 70 percent
100 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of your motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a turn?

options.text: Speed up.
Slow down.
Move your shoulders to match the turn's angle.
Sit up as high as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Before entering a turn, slow down. Release the throttle and apply the brakes if needed.

questions.question: What should you do in a slow, tight turn?

options.text: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
Lean at the same angle as the motorcycle.
Lean in the opposite direction of the motorcycle and turn.
Keep the motorcycle upright while your body leans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, lean with your motorcycle. In slow, tight turns, keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.

questions.question: Which part of the lane should always be avoided?

options.text: The left side
The center
The right side
No part should always be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: No part should always be avoided.
questions.explanation: No lane position is always best, and no lane position should always be avoided. Choose a position based on your riding conditions.

questions.question: How do you get maximum straight-line braking?

options.text: Use the rear brake only.
Use the front brake only.
Use both brakes.
Use the rear brake while downshifting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes fully without locking either wheel. Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks that run parallel to the road, what should you do?

options.text: Cross at a 90-degree angle.
Avoid crossing them.
Cross at a 45-degree angle.
Cross slowly and carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross at a 45-degree angle.
questions.explanation: Cross the tracks at an angle of at least 45 degrees, then turn quickly and sharply. If you cross slowly, the tracks could catch your tires and throw you off balance.

questions.question: If your motorcycle has convex mirrors and you are new to them, why should you practice?

options.text: Most people are not used to using mirrors.
They make objects look farther away than they really are.
They make objects look closer than they really are.
It is hard to remember to check mirrors while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make objects look farther away than they really are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. However, they make objects look farther away than they actually are. Get used to your mirrors before riding.

questions.question: If you lock the rear tire on a surface with good traction, what should you do?

options.text: Release and re-apply the rear brake.
Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release it and use only the front brake.
Release it and use both brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If you lock the rear brake on a surface with good traction, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can still steer your motorcycle with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: How do you swerve correctly?

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Press the handgrip toward the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip away from the direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip toward the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: Press the handgrip on the side you want to turn. Press the opposite handgrip to return to your original direction once you clear the hazard.

questions.question: To accommodate a passenger, you may need to:

options.text: Adjust the shocks.
Adjust the handlebars.
Adjust the brakes.
Adjust the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Adjust the shocks.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. You may need to adjust the shocks before carrying a passenger. The motorcycle will sit at a different angle, so also adjust the headlight and mirrors.

questions.question: If your front tire locks while braking, you should:

options.text: Keep the brake engaged until you come to a full stop.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.
Release the brake lever and use only the rear brake.
Release the brake lever until the tire regains traction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the brake lever until the tire regains traction.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the brake lever. Let the tire grip the road again. Then reapply the brake.

questions.question: When it is raining, it is usually best to:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off to the side of the road until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Increase your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Wet pavement is very slippery when rain first starts. Oil from cars has not yet washed away. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left track is often the safest choice, but this can vary.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should position themselves:

options.text: Just behind the leader.
In front of the group.
At the tail end of the group.
Beside the leader.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should position themselves just behind the leader. This allows experienced riders to watch them without having the inexperienced rider lead the group.
